scope: P1.2 maintenance file-authorization policy: unit/boundary evidence only. NOT a GUI approval flow, NOT an OS sandbox, NOT extension activation, and it does not close the TOCTOU window between a permission check and the executor's open/write.

addedThisRound: delete is classified as delete and actually deletes
an unparseable patch authorizes nothing and changes nothing
a caller cannot mislabel a delete by supplying its own patch plan
a move authorizes both the source and the destination
a missing or non-Map plan denies and never reaches the approver

newDesignNotRecoveredOriginal: checkPermission appears 0 times in recovered/shuncode-extension/src/*.ts and the original callback has no operation parameter. The operation-aware contract is new maintenance design.
guarantees: literal true only; false/truthy-non-boolean/throw/reject all deny
grant keyed by owner + tool + operation + realpath
bounded TTL; workspace-roots snapshot change invalidates
revokeOwner for session teardown; close() denies and clears
cancellation checked before and after the host await
knownLimitations: TOCTOU window between check and open remains
grants are cached within TTL because applyPatch runs preflight twice
modern-era owners have no teardown hook and rely on expiry alone
supplying the callback downgrades find/search from ripgrep to the Node walker
native-chat is a fallback constant, not an authenticated subject
Two surviving mutants (M12, M13) are equivalent mutants, proven by differential probe rather than assumed; see mutationTesting.round3.equivalentMutants.

initiallySurvived: cache key without operation (test crossed tools, so keys differed anyway)
removed pre-await closed check (masked by the post-await check)
mutationTesting.resolution: Both were test gaps; assertions were strengthened rather than the finding softened.

round3.target: plan derivation and the no-plan guard

killed.mutation: do not record the move destination
classification catch returns true instead of false

equivalentMutants.mutation: on derivation failure set resolvedPlan = undefined instead of an empty Map
equivalentMutants.verdict: EQUIVALENT MUTANT, not a gap in the tests and not a vulnerability.
equivalentMutants.proof: A differential probe recorded every observable output (callback return value, thrown code, approver call count, isError, file contents) for plans undefined/null/{}/empty Map/wrong-path and for two end-to-end derivation failures. Baseline and mutant outputs were byte-identical: all deny, approver consulted 0 times, files intact.
equivalentMutants.why: Both an empty Map and a missing plan reach the same guard and produce the same denial, so no test can distinguish them by observable behaviour.

equivalentMutants.mutation: remove the explicit "plan is not a Map" guard
equivalentMutants.verdict: EQUIVALENT MUTANT under the current code, retained deliberately as defence in depth.
equivalentMutants.proof: Same differential probe: outputs identical to baseline.
equivalentMutants.why: The lookup below the guard uses a Map-shaped access that already yields undefined for a non-Map plan, which denies. The explicit guard is redundant TODAY; it is kept so that a future refactor of the lookup cannot silently turn "no plan" into "no checks".

round3.honestyNote: These two mutants are reported as surviving rather than being papered over with a test that asserts an internal detail purely to force a kill. A test that cannot observe a behavioural difference would be testing the implementation, not the contract.

crossPlatformDefectFoundByCI.symptom: ubuntu-24.04 passed; windows-2022 and windows-cmd-conda failed in npm test.
crossPlatformDefectFoundByCI.cause: Executors realpath() workspace roots before calling checkPermission, but patchPlan was keyed by the host's raw spelling. Windows mkdtemp returns an 8.3 short name that realpath expands, so no key matched and every apply_patch checkpoint was denied.
crossPlatformDefectFoundByCI.fix: canonicalizePatchPlan resolves plan keys like the executors do; case-folded index on win32.
crossPlatformDefectFoundByCI.regressionTest: symlink/junction root case, skipped explicitly where unsupported

releaseGate.reason: The policy is exercised only by maintenance tests. No real host UI constructs it yet, and the shipped portable bundle does not contain it.

planDerivation.change: The apply_patch authorization plan is now derived inside the policy module from the patch text, using the original parsePatch + resolveExistingPath/resolveNewPath exported by reconstructed/bridge-core/src/apply-patch.js. It is no longer supplied by the caller.
whyTwoReasons: Correctness: a caller-supplied plan had to spell paths exactly as the executors resolve them. It did not on Windows (mkdtemp short names expand under realpath), which shipped a Windows-only defect caught by CI run 35351320215.

Trust boundary: a wrong or hostile caller could mislabel an operation, e.g. present a Delete File patch while declaring the path as "update", so a host that only granted modify rights would have destroyed the file.
planDerivation.apiChange: invokeFileToolWithPolicy no longer accepts a patchPlan parameter. createPermissionCallback still accepts one so unit tests can inject a plan directly.
planDerivation.failClosed: If derivation throws, the plan becomes an empty Map and every path is unclassifiable, so nothing is authorized. The executor re-parses and reports the authoritative error.

hostileProbe.scenario: Caller passes patchPlan [secretPath, "update"] while the patch body is "*** Delete File: secret.txt".
hostileProbe.beforeChange: Policy would have seen operation "modify" and a modify-only grant would have authorized the delete.
hostileProbe.note: The forged plan is ignored entirely; the operation comes from the real parse.
